summary: Anthropic released Claude Opus 4.7, a general-availability model upgrade with improved coding, vision, agentic and long-context capabilities at the same price as Opus 4.6.

mechanisms.reason: The announcement describes a step change in coding, reasoning, and multimodal capability over the prior flagship model.
mechanisms.quote: Opus 4.7 is a notable improvement on Opus 4.6 in advanced software engineering, with particular gains on the most difficult tasks.

mechanisms.reason: Multiple partner quotes describe Opus 4.7 enabling longer-horizon, more autonomous agent workflows with fewer tool errors and less supervision.
mechanisms.quote: Claude Opus 4.7 takes long-horizon autonomy to a new level in Devin. It works coherently for hours, pushes through hard problems rather than giving up.

mechanisms.reason: Higher-resolution image support and increased test-time reasoning/output tokens raise per-request memory and context demands.
mechanisms.quote: it can accept images up to 2,576 pixels on the long edge (~3.75 megapixels), more than three times as many as prior Claude models.

mechanisms.reason: The model thinks more at higher effort levels and produces more output tokens per task, increasing aggregate inference volume even as efficiency improves.
mechanisms.quote: Opus 4.7 thinks more at higher effort levels, particularly on later turns in agentic settings. This improves its reliability on hard problems, but it does mean it produces more output tokens.

categories.reason: The model is distributed through major cloud platforms, reinforcing their role as both AI builders and buyers.
categories.quote: Opus 4.7 is available today across all Claude products and our API, Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud\u2019s Vertex AI, and Microsoft Foundry.

notable_reason: A frontier lab flagship model upgrade with broad enterprise adoption signals, agentic and long-context capability gains, and unchanged pricing, relevant to inference demand and memory/context intensity trends.
